title: Princeton Public Library
venue_description:
Princeton Public Library

A few steps from Palmer Square in the heart of downtown Princeton, the Princeton Public Library is far more than a place to check out books. Its glass-walled Community Room and outdoor Hinds Plaza have become a low-key but genuine home for the town's amateur musicians, hosting a periodic Open Acoustic Jam that draws singers, guitarists, ukulele players, and anyone who wants to make music together in a completely informal, alcohol-free setting.

Atmosphere and Setting

The library's Community Room is bright, modern, and welcoming rather than a typical bar-room jam space. Chord charts and lyrics are projected on a large screen, or followed along on a phone through the NJAMP Songbook app, so the emphasis is on group participation rather than performance. It is an easy entry point for musicians who might feel intimidated by a bar-based open mic.

The Open Acoustic Jam

Held periodically throughout the year in partnership with NJ Acoustic Music in the Park (NJAMP), the Open Acoustic Jam runs on select Sunday afternoons from 3:00 PM to 4:30 PM. Led by longtime NJAMP organizers Mike and Judy Seidel, the session welcomes acoustic guitar, ukulele, violin, resonator, tambourine, and voice at every skill level. No registration or performance experience is required — attendees can sing along, play along, or simply listen and clap.

Other Programming

Beyond the jam sessions, the library has also hosted outdoor Listen Local open mic afternoons on Hinds Plaza in partnership with the Einstein Alley Musicians Collaborative, giving local original and cover musicians a public stage in the middle of downtown. The library's event calendar is worth checking regularly for the next installment of either series.

Good to Know

Princeton Public Library is located at 65 Witherspoon Street, Princeton, NJ. Because the acoustic jam runs on an occasional rather than weekly schedule, check the library's online events calendar to confirm the next date before visiting.

title: Arts Council of Princeton
venue_description:
Arts Council of Princeton

Housed in the Paul Robeson Center for the Arts on Witherspoon Street, the Arts Council of Princeton is the town's community arts hub — a nonprofit with galleries, classrooms, and a black-box performance space called the Solley Theater. Once a month that theater turns into Princeton's longest-running open mic stage, Cafe Improv, now in its fourth decade.

Atmosphere and Setting

The Solley Theater is an intimate, listening-room-style black-box space rather than a bar or restaurant, giving performers a real stage, sound support, and an attentive audience. The vibe is warm and low-pressure — the kind of room built to encourage first-timers alongside seasoned local performers.

Cafe Improv

Cafe Improv is held monthly on a Saturday evening from 7:00 PM to 10:00 PM. For more than 30 years the show, hosted by John Irving and Tom Florek, has connected beginning and professional performers across music, poetry, comedy, and more. Admission is a modest $2 for the general public and $1 for Arts Council members, and performers can register in advance at cafeimprov.com or sign up at the door.

Other Programming

The Arts Council also hosts the monthly Story & Verse poetry and spoken-word open mic in the same Solley Theater, along with a full slate of gallery exhibitions, classes, and community events throughout the year, making the Paul Robeson Center a steady gathering point for Princeton's performing and visual artists alike.

Good to Know

The Arts Council of Princeton is located at 102 Witherspoon Street, Princeton, NJ. Because Cafe Improv runs monthly rather than weekly, check the Arts Council's calendar or cafeimprov.com to confirm the next date.
